question: What does the "Restoration" refer to in the teachings of the LDS Church?
answer: The return, begun by Joseph Smith, of the authentic priesthood power, spiritual gifts, ordinances, living prophets and revelation of the primitive Church of Christ, which the church teaches were lost after the deaths of Jesus and his apostles.
source_title: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
evidence: The LDS Church teaches that, subsequent to the death of Jesus and his original apostles, his church, along with the authority to act in Jesus Christ's name and the church's attendant spiritual gifts, were lost, due to a combination of external persecutions and internal heresies. The "Restoration"—as begun by Joseph Smith and embodied in the church itself—refers to a return of the authentic priesthood power, spiritual gifts, ordinances, living prophets and revelation of the primitive Church of Christ.

question: How is a new president of the LDS Church chosen when the current president dies, and what effect has this had on church leadership?
answer: By convention the longest-tenured apostle becomes president; because apostles serve for life, this has made the leadership increasingly elderly.
source_title: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
evidence: When a president dies, his successor is chosen from the remaining apostles. By longstanding convention, the longest-tenured apostle becomes the next president of the church. In recent years, this process has contributed to the church's leadership being of increasingly advanced age, given that apostles serve for life.

question: What substances does the Word of Wisdom ask Latter-day Saints to abstain from?
answer: Alcohol, coffee, tea, tobacco, and illicit or harmful substances.
source_title: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
evidence: The LDS Church asks its members to adhere to a dietary code called the Word of Wisdom, in which they abstain from the consumption of alcohol, coffee, tea, tobacco, and illicit or harmful substances.

question: How did the status of the Word of Wisdom change from when Joseph Smith published it to the presidency of Heber J. Grant?
answer: It began as advice whose violation did not restrict membership, but Heber J. Grant made obeying it a requirement for worship inside temples.
source_title: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
evidence: When Joseph Smith published the Word of Wisdom in 1833, it was considered only advice; violation did not restrict church membership. During the 1890s, though, church leaders started emphasizing the Word of Wisdom more. In 1921, church president Heber J. Grant made obeying the Word of Wisdom a requirement to engage in worship inside of the faith's temples.

question: Where do the terms "Mormon" and "Mormonism" come from?
answer: From the name of the Book of Mormon.
source_title: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
evidence: The Book of Mormon is a foundational sacred book for the church; the terms "Mormon" and "Mormonism" come from the name of the book itself.

question: Why is the LDS Church's scriptural canon described as "open"?
answer: Because of the Latter-day Saint belief in continuous revelation; scripture can be added with the common consent of the church's membership.
evidence: The scriptural canon is "open" due to the Latter-day Saint belief in continuous revelation. Additions can be made to the scriptural canon with the "common consent" of the church's membership.

question: According to Harold B. Lee, how should church members judge a statement by a church authority that contradicts the standard works?
answer: They may know it is false, whatever the speaker's position, because the standard works are the standard measure of all that men teach.
evidence: And if he says something that contradicts what is found in the standard works (I think that is why we call them "standard"—it is the standard measure of all that men teach), you may know by that same token that it is false; regardless of the position of the man who says it.

question: Why do Latter-day Saints accept the Bible as the word of God only "as far as it is translated correctly"?
answer: Because they believe errors, omissions and mistranslations exist even in the earliest Biblical manuscripts and have led to incorrect interpretations.
evidence: Though the Bible is part of the LDS Church's canon and members believe it to be the word of God, they believe that errors, omissions, and mistranslations are present in even the earliest known Biblical manuscripts. They state that the errors in the Bible have led to incorrect interpretations of certain passages. Thus, as Joseph Smith explained, the church believes the Bible to be the word of God "as far as it is translated correctly".

question: How does the canon of the Bickertonites and the Church of Christ (Temple Lot) differ from the LDS Church's standard works?
answer: Both reject the Doctrine and Covenants and the Pearl of Great Price, accepting the King James Bible and the Book of Mormon as their scripture.
evidence: Like the Bickertonites, the Church of Christ (Temple Lot) rejects the D&C and the Pearl of Great Price, as well as the Joseph Smith Translation of the Bible, preferring to use only the King James Bible and the Book of Mormon as doctrinal standards.

question: Why is the Song of Solomon not part of the LDS Church's canon, even though it is printed in the church's Bible?
answer: Because the manuscripts of the Joseph Smith Translation state that the Songs of Solomon are not inspired scripture.
evidence: The manuscripts of the Joseph Smith Translation of the Bible state that "the Songs of Solomon are not inspired scripture," and therefore it is not included in the LDS Church's canon and is rarely studied by its members. However, it is still printed in every version of the KJV published by the church.

question: What led to the death of Joseph Smith and his brother Hyrum?
answer: After Smith had the press of the dissident Nauvoo Expositor destroyed, he was charged with riot and then treason, and while in state custody a mob attacked the jail and killed both brothers.
source_title: History of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
evidence: The destruction of the press led to charges of riot against Smith and other members of the council. After Smith surrendered on the charges, he was also charged with treason against Illinois. While in state custody, he and his brother Hyrum Smith, who was second in line to the church presidency, were killed in a firefight with an angry mob attacking the jail on June 27, 1844.

question: What was the outcome of the Utah War for Brigham Young's role as governor?
answer: The governorship of Utah Territory passed from Brigham Young to Alfred Cumming, an outsider appointed by President James Buchanan.
source_title: History of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
evidence: The result of the Utah War was the succeeding of the governorship of the Utah territory from Brigham Young to Alfred Cumming, an outsider appointed by President James Buchanan.

question: Why did church president Joseph F. Smith issue the Second Manifesto?
answer: In response to the Senate hearings on seating Reed Smoot, which raised doubts about whether polygamy had truly been abandoned under the 1890 Manifesto.
source_title: History of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
evidence: However, the hearings raised controversy as to whether polygamy had actually been abandoned as claimed in the 1890 Manifesto, and whether the LDS Church continued to exercise influence on Utah politics. In response to these hearings, church president Joseph F. Smith issued a Second Manifesto denying that any post-Manifesto marriages had the church's sanction, and announcing that those entering such marriages in the future would be excommunicated.

question: What change did the church's 1981 edition of the standard works make to a Book of Mormon passage about the Lamanites?
answer: It replaced the word "white" with "pure" in the passage saying Lamanites will become "white and delightsome" after accepting the gospel.
source_title: History of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
evidence: In 1981, the church published a new LDS edition of the Standard Works that changed a passage in "The Book of Mormon" that Lamanites (considered by many Latter-day Saints to be Native Americans) will "become white and delightsome" after accepting the gospel of Jesus Christ. Instead of continuing the original reference to skin color, the new edition replaced the word "white" with the word "pure".

question: How did the 1967 discovery of the Joseph Smith papyri affect views of his translation of the Book of Abraham?
answer: Egyptologists identified them as the Book of the Dead and their translations disagreed with Smith's, forcing many apologists to moderate the view that his translations were literal one-to-one translations.
source_title: History of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
evidence: Analyzed by Egyptologists, the manuscripts were identified as "The Book of the Dead", an ancient Egyptian funerary text. Moreover, the scholars' translations of the scrolls disagreed with Smith's purported translation. This discovery forced many Mormon apologists to moderate the earlier prevailing view that Smith's translations were literal one-to-one translations.
